issue.summary: Friendly Names for Attributes Not Displayed Consistently in Web Editor
issue.description:
Consolidated Jira description and reviewer scope:
- Full Tags View shows the original attribute name.
- Condition Attributes panel does not show the friendly name.
- Right Panel loses the friendly name after the attribute is applied.
- Preserve the complete custom and built-in fallback rule.
- Cover add, update, and remove while the editor remains open.
- Discover future valid conditional attributes from supported configuration.
- Cover the effective label seen by each signed-in author without profile leakage.
- Cover the Use only above attributes restriction.
- Preserve mappings through upgrade.
- Do not regress element friendly names.
- Decide whether Condition Presets are in scope.
- Decide whether the DITAVAL attribute dropdown is in scope.
- Decide whether Preview is in scope.

rag_probes: In AEM Guides XML Editor, how are friendly display names for DITA attributes configured, and is the configuration stored per user, in the global profile, or in a folder profile?

Which AEM Guides authoring surfaces are documented to use a configured friendly display name for an attribute, including Full Tags View, the Condition Attributes panel, the Right Panel, condition presets, the DITAVAL attribute dropdown, and Preview?
How does AEM Guides use /apps/fmdita/config/condAttrList.csv, /libs/fmdita/config/condAttrList.csv, and the legacy condAttrList.xml when a custom conditional attribute is added?
What does the AEM Guides XML Editor setting 'Use only above attributes' do, especially for attributes already applied to an element?

rag_probe_results.finding: General XML Editor configuration is documented at global-profile and folder-profile levels; friendly attribute label storage is not explicitly documented.
Condition Presets are documented as an attribute-selection surface, but friendly-name behavior is not documented on any listed surface.
The shipped conditional list and version-dependent legacy XML are documented; exact precedence comes from inspected Starling code.
The answer relies on analogy with the element restriction and labels the already-applied attribute behavior unverified.

source_acceptance_criteria: AC-01: Full Tags View shows the workspace friendly name for every allowed attribute.
AC-02: Built-in conditional attributes show their configured friendly name or default label without malformed text.
AC-03: The Right Panel keeps the friendly name during selection and after the attribute is applied.
AC-04: An unmapped custom attribute shows its raw name, an unmapped built-in shows its default label, and no label is blank.
AC-05: Adding, editing, or removing a mapping updates already-rendered rows and an open dropdown without reload; removal restores fallback.
AC-06: A valid conditional attribute added to the supported conditional list is discovered from the active profile and schema without a product-code change.

operational_contract.reason: This feature resolves labels during synchronous editor rendering and configuration save; it has no job, queue, listener, retry, migration, repair, or long-running execution contract.

feature_classification.rationale: The ticket changes how one configured attribute label is rendered across multiple UI consumers and configuration scopes.

trigger: An author opens an attribute-rendering surface or an administrator saves an attribute-label setting.
operations: Resolve the effective profile mapping, apply raw-name fallback, and render the attribute label.
outputs: Visible attribute label in each in-scope editor surface
affected_state: Editor label models and profile configuration
write_paths: Editor configuration save writes mappings and the restriction flag for the active profile.
read_paths: Editor startup loads ditaAttributes mappings and constraint state.
Conditional setup reads the effective conditional attribute values.
update_paths: Open Tag View receives an attribute friendly-name update when the cross-package command exists.
fallback_paths: Missing friendly name falls back to the raw name.
Missing folder profile falls back to global-profile configuration.
Missing apps conditional list falls back to libs.
versioned_models: Pre-upgrade and post-upgrade Editor profile configuration
constraints: Only DTD-valid attributes are offered for the selected element.
Already-applied attributes remain visible when choices are restricted.
unknowns: Friendly-name scope for Condition Presets, DITAVAL, and Preview
Target build support for the guarded update command
Supported legacy XML and CSV precedence contract

facts.fact: Jira requests one effective friendly name across three named editor surfaces.
The cached PR ref adds friendly lookup and fallback in the attribute, condition, and applied-row models.
Current configuration code saves attribute mappings under an active folder profile with global fallback.
Starling checks the apps overlay before libs and legacy XML before CSV.

CLEAN_PRE_FIX_STATE.behavior: A saved mapping can exist before the fix while the affected surfaces still render the raw name.

STATE_CREATED_BY_FIXED_CODE.behavior: A mapping saved by the fixed build should render its friendly name and remain readable after reopen or upgrade.

STATE_CREATED_BY_BUGGY_OLD_CODE.behavior: The Jira evidence shows a display mismatch, not a corrupted mapping; the existing mapping is reused after the fix.

evidence: Jira attachment GUIDES-49507 shows the mapping saved as product to category while the UI renders Product or product.

named_artifacts.premise: Conditional setup seeds eight fixed names before adding runtime values.
Editor settings serialize friendly-name mappings and the restriction flag.
The effective conditional list uses apps-over-libs lookup and checks legacy XML before CSV.
